newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian central bank foreign assets rise in September.
newsitem.headline: Latvian central bank foreign assets rise in September.

text.p: Foreign assets of the central bank of Latvia rose in September to 311.1 million lats from 301 million lats the previous month while currency in circulation rose to 261 million lats from 252.8 million lats.
The bank said in its monthly bulletin that it bought 3.8 million lats of foreign convertible currency in September, half of the amount bought in August.

It said lat interests rates continued to decline during the month, with the average rate on the interbank market falling to 7.5 percent versus 9.8 percent in August. Credits granted in the interbank market fell by 15 percent to 54.1 million lats.
The central bank also said that deposits in banks in September maintained their recent rise, hitting 357.1 million lats after 341.4 million lats in August.
Stability has gradually returned to Latvia after it was last year hit by one of eastern Europe's worst banking crises, sparked by the closure of what its largest bank, Banka Baltiya.
